positions.stakeholder_concern: Current expectations allow clinicians to comment on or dismiss inaccurate or irrelevant AI outputs, but there is no traceability of what happens to that clinician feedback afterward, so it may not inform model or content improvements.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require "full loop" auditability in which clinician responses, actions, and comments on AI outputs are audited to show whether they were used to adjust the model, adjust knowledge delivery, or were dismissed, with a documented reason recorded for dismissals.

gap_explanations.human_ai_system_performance: The comment treats clinician interaction with and correction of AI outputs as monitoring evidence that should be systematically captured rather than looking only at device output performance.
gap_explanations.distributed_accountability: It asks for a documented record of who acted on or dismissed clinician feedback, making responsibility for closing the feedback loop traceable.

positions.public_summary: Commenter accepts postmarket monitoring involving clinician review but asks FDA to go further and require "full loop" auditability: clinician comments, actions, and dismissals of AI outputs should be tracked to show whether they changed the model or knowledge delivery, with reasons recorded for dismissals.
positions.source_passage: While current regulations require that HCP be able to comment or dismiss irrelevant or inaccurate AI model outputs they have been presented with, the regulations should require "full loop" auditability whereby HCP responses, actions or comments on AI outputs are audited for how those response where used to either adjust hte AI model, adjust knowledge delivery or dismissed.  If HCP responses are dismissed, there should be a reason noted.
